ostrzezenia.tekst: Drying and cooking do not destroy the toxins of poisonous mushrooms, and only an expert can tell edible species from poisonous ones. [T:SUS-035]

akapity: NCHFP warns: do not can wild mushrooms; its tested canning process is only for small to medium-size cultivated mushrooms with unopened caps. [T:ACI-030]
Mushrooms pickled in vinegar and processed in jars in a boiling-water bath are canned mushrooms, so this warning applies to them too. [T:-]
The FDA list gives mushrooms a pH of about 6.00–6.70, while acid foods are foods with a natural pH of 4.6 or lower. [T:ACI-159,ACI-001]
Most mixtures of low-acid and acid foods have a pH above 4.6 unless the recipe contains enough lemon juice, citric acid or vinegar. [T:ACI-006]
In Poland, the most frequent and most dangerous mushroom poisonings are caused by the death cap, which is mistaken for edible species such as the parasol mushroom. [T:SUS-141]
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for wild mushrooms in vinegar from a checked source. [T:-]
